About

Hi! I’m Francesco Alessandro Pinto, a researcher in Software Engineering at the SeSa Lab of the University of Salerno, where I also earned both my B.Sc. and M.Sc. in Computer Science.

My work sits where Software Engineering for AI (SE4AI) meets AI for Software Engineering (AI4SE): how to build better ML-enabled systems, and how AI, especially Large Language Models, can help developers write better code. My bachelor’s thesis introduced CAMILLE, a chatbot that helps ML engineers detect and refactor ML-specific code smells; my master’s thesis studied how the readability of developers’ prompts relates to the quality of the code LLMs generate.

When I’m not staring at code, I’m probably swimming laps, kneading pizza dough, adding bricks to a LEGO castle or starting yet another Skyrim playthrough.

Currently

  • Brainstorming new experiments to run (the whiteboard is losing the battle).
  • Working on code smell detection using Neurosymbolic AI.
  • Counting down the days to Avengers: Doomsday.

Research Interests

Software Engineering for AI

How ML-enabled systems are designed, built and maintained, and which quality issues make them different from traditional software.

AI for Software Engineering

Using AI and LLMs to support developers, from conversational assistants to automated refactoring suggestions.

Code Quality & Code Smells

Detecting and removing code smells, with a focus on ML-specific ones, to keep software maintainable over time.

Developer-LLM Interaction

How developers prompt LLMs, and how prompt quality and readability affect the quality of the generated code.

Neurosymbolic AI

Combining neural models with symbolic reasoning to build more reliable and explainable software analysis tools.

Empirical Software Engineering

Data-driven studies of real software and developers, backed by sound statistical analysis.
